newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada cancer rate expected to jump this year.
newsitem.headline: Canada cancer rate expected to jump this year.

text.p: About 130,800 Canadians will be diagnosed with cancer this year, and almost 61,000 Canadian will die of the disease, Statistics Canada said on Thursday.
The number of people to be diagnosed with the often deadly disease is expected to be 36 percent higher than the 96,518 cases reported a decade ago, Statscan said.
The number of deaths in 1997 will be 25 percent higher than in 1987, the agency said.
Lung cancer is the main culprit.
"Lung cancer will kill more individuals than any other form of cancer in 1997," Statscan said. Almost 11,000 men and 6,300 women will die of lung cancer this year.
The agency said the rise in the numbers stems from Canada's growing and aging population.

Prostrate cancer will likely be the most commonly diagnosed cancer for men, with an anticipated 19,800 new cases -- more than double the level a decade ago. For women, the most frequent diagnosis will be breast cancer, with an expected 18,400 new cases.
Cancer in Canada primarily effects older people. About 71 percent of new cases and 80 percent of deaths in 1997 are expected to be among people over 60.
